title: African Water Facility (AWF) 2026 Call for Proposals: Apply for Up to EUR 1 Million in Grant Funding to Strengthen Africa’s Water and Sanitation Investment Pipeline
summary: The African Water Facility (AWF) has officially launched its 2026 Call for Proposals (CfP) under the AWF 2026–2030 Strategy , providing an exciting funding opportunity for eligible institutions across Africa to develop high-impact, investment-ready water and sanitation projects.The initiative seeks to strengthen Africa s water and sanitation investment pipeline by supporting innovative projects capable of attracting downstream financing while improving access to safe water, enhancing sanitation services, strengthening climate resilience, and promoting sustainable and inclusive development. Administered by the African Development Bank (AfDB) on behalf of the African Ministers Council on Water (AMCOW) , the African Water Facility continues to play a critical role in transforming project concepts into bankable investments that deliver lasting benefits to communities across the continent. Organizations involved in water security, sanitation, public infrastructure, and institutional development are encouraged to submit concept notes before the application deadline. About the African Water Facility (AWF) The African Water Facility is a specialized initiative established by the African Ministers Council on Water (AMCOW) and administered by the African Development Bank Group. Its mission is to mobilize investments that improve water security and sanitation services throughout Africa by supporting the preparation of quality projects that are attractive to investors and development partners. Rather than financing large-scale infrastructure directly, the Facility focuses on helping organizations prepare strong, investment-ready projects capable of attracting significant future financing from governments, development finance institutions, and private investors. Through the 2026–2030 Strategy, AWF aims to accelerate progress toward sustainable water management while contributing to climate resilience and improved livelihoods across the continent. Purpose of the 2026 Call for Proposals The 2026 Call for Proposals is designed to build a stronger pipeline of bankable water and sanitation projects throughout Africa. The initiative seeks projects that can: Accelerate access to investment financing. Improve water and sanitation services. Strengthen climate resilience. Promote sustainable infrastructure development. Support inclusive economic growth. Enhance institutional capacity. Generate long-term development impact. Attract downstream public and private investment. Successful projects will contribute to transforming innovative project concepts into investment-ready operations capable of securing additional financing. Funding Available The African Water Facility will provide grant financing to selected projects. AWF Contribution Each successful project may receive: Grant funding of up to EUR 1 million . The funding is intended to support project preparation activities that increase investment readiness and improve the likelihood of securing larger financing for implementation. Priority Areas The 2026 Call for Proposals focuses on six strategic priority areas. 1. Project Preparation and Investment Readiness Projects that strengthen technical, financial, environmental, and institutional preparation to make investments bankable. 2. Climate-Resilient Water and Sanitation Systems Projects that improve the resilience of water supply and sanitation infrastructure against climate-related risks such as droughts, floods, and changing weather patterns. 3. Innovative Financing and Catalytic Investments Initiatives that introduce innovative financial approaches capable of mobilizing additional investment from development partners and the private sector. 4. Governance and Institutional Strengthening Projects that improve governance systems, institutional effectiveness, planning, management, and regulatory capacity within the water and sanitation sector. 5. Inclusive and Sustainable Service Delivery Projects designed to expand equitable access to quality water and sanitation services while ensuring long-term sustainability. 6. Sanitation Sector Transformation Innovative initiatives that improve sanitation infrastructure, services, planning, and investment to address sanitation challenges across Africa. Who Should Apply? The Call for Proposals welcomes applications from eligible institutions operating within Africa, including: Regional Member Countries (RMCs) Public institutions Water utilities River basin organizations Other eligible entities involved in water and sanitation development Organizations with strong project concepts that can be developed into investment-ready operations are encouraged to apply. Geographic Scope The funding opportunity is exclusively focused on projects implemented within Africa . Applicants should demonstrate how their proposed project contributes to improving water security and sanitation outcomes on the continent. Why Apply? Participating organizations can benefit from several advantages, including: Access to grant financing of up to EUR 1 million. Support in preparing investment-ready projects. Increased opportunities to mobilize larger downstream financing. Strengthened institutional and technical capacity. Improved project bankability. Enhanced climate resilience. Better water and sanitation service delivery. Contribution to sustainable and inclusive development across Africa. Required Application Documents Applicants should prepare the following documents: Completed Concept Note. Official AWF Concept Note Template. Supporting documentation required under the Call for Proposals. Applicants are encouraged to carefully review the complete Call for Proposals before preparing their submissions. How to Apply To submit a proposal, applicants should follow these steps: Step 1 Review the full 2026 Call for Proposals to understand the eligibility requirements, funding priorities, and evaluation criteria. Step 2 Download the official Concept Note Template . Step 3 Prepare a high-quality concept note that clearly demonstrates: Project objectives. Expected development impact. Investment readiness. Alignment with AWF priority areas. Potential to mobilize downstream financing. Step 4 Submit the completed Concept Note before the application deadline to: African Water Facility (AWF), African Development Bank Group Email: africanwaterfacility@afdb.org CC: Mr. Samuel Blazyk, Officer in Charge, AWF Ms. Hellen Njiwa, Principal Monitoring, Evaluation and Project Portfolio Management Officer Ms. Diane Arjoon, Principal Rural Water Security Officer Important Funding Information Funding Type Grant Financing Maximum Grant Amount Up to EUR 1 million per project. Geographic Coverage Africa Eligible Applicants Regional Member Countries, public institutions, utilities, basin organizations, and other eligible entities. Learn more about the opportunity HERE Application Deadline Deadline: 10 September 2026 Applicants are encouraged to begin preparing their concept notes early to allow sufficient time for developing strong, investment-ready proposals before submission. Conclusion The African Water Facility 2026 Call for Proposals presents an outstanding opportunity for African governments, public institutions, utilities, and water sector organizations to secure grant funding that transforms promising project ideas into bankable investments. By supporting project preparation, climate resilience, governance reforms, innovative financing, and sustainable service delivery, the Facility is helping build a stronger pipeline of water and sanitation investments across Africa. Eligible organizations with innovative, high-impact project concepts should take advantage of this opportunity to access up to EUR 1 million in grant financing and contribute to improving water security, sanitation services, and sustainable development across the continent. Interested applicants should review the Call for Proposals, prepare a compelling Concept Note, and submit their application before 10 September 2026 . title: Become a Churchill Fellow 2026–2027: Applications Open Soon for Changemakers Seeking Global Solutions to Local Challenges
summary: Individuals who are passionate about creating meaningful change in the issues they care about will soon have an opportunity to join one of the world s most respected leadership and research fellowships. The Churchill Fellowship offers motivated individuals the chance to explore innovative ideas, learn from leading experts across the globe, and return home with practical knowledge that can transform communities, organizations, and public policy. The Churchill Fellowship is widely recognized as a unique opportunity that empowers people from diverse backgrounds to investigate solutions to pressing social, economic, environmental, educational, cultural, and health-related challenges. Rather than focusing solely on academic qualifications, the Fellowship emphasizes passion, leadership potential, and a commitment to creating lasting impact. Applications for the next Churchill Fellowship programme will officially open on 1 September 2026 and close on 20 October 2026 . Individuals interested in becoming Fellows are encouraged to prepare early and sign up for application alerts. What is the Churchill Fellowship? A Churchill Fellowship is a prestigious opportunity that enables individuals to explore new ideas by connecting with leading professionals and organizations around the world. Fellows investigate innovative approaches to challenges affecting their communities and bring back practical knowledge that can be adapted and implemented for positive change. Unlike many traditional academic fellowships, the Churchill Fellowship focuses on real-world impact. Fellows are expected to identify an issue they care deeply about, explore international best practices, and apply what they learn to improve their communities, sectors, or professions. The Fellowship is designed for individuals who want to: Drive meaningful social change. Learn from global experts. Develop innovative solutions. Strengthen leadership capacity. Create long-term community impact. Expand professional networks. Inspire policy and practice improvements. It is considered a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity for individuals determined to make a difference. Why Become a Churchill Fellow? The Fellowship exists to support individuals who have a genuine desire to solve problems rather than simply study them. Fellows investigate how similar challenges are addressed in other countries and return with ideas that can be adapted within their own communities. Participants become part of a respected network of Fellows working across numerous disciplines and sectors. The Fellowship provides opportunities to: Learn directly from world-leading professionals. Build international partnerships. Explore innovative practices. Strengthen leadership skills. Develop evidence-based solutions. Share knowledge with communities. Influence policy discussions. Improve services and systems. Create sustainable social impact. Join a lifelong network of Churchill Fellows. Areas of Research and Interest Churchill Fellows undertake research across a broad range of topics. Current areas highlighted by the Fellowship include: Arts and Communities Arts and Culture Children and Young People Children in Care Climate Change Community and Citizenship COVID-19 Creative Ageing Disability Early Years Intervention Economy and Enterprise Education and Skills Emergency Response Enterprise and Social Impact Environment and Resources Equity, Diversity and Inclusion In total, Fellows contribute research across dozens of thematic areas, demonstrating the Fellowship s commitment to addressing complex global challenges through innovative thinking and practical solutions. A Fellowship Focused on Impact The Churchill Fellowship is not simply about international travel or professional development. It is about equipping people to return with practical ideas that improve lives. Successful Fellows often contribute by: Improving public services. Strengthening community programmes. Developing new educational approaches. Supporting vulnerable populations. Advancing environmental sustainability. Promoting inclusion and diversity. Encouraging innovation in business and enterprise. Supporting cultural development. Influencing national and local policy. Building stronger communities. The Fellowship encourages participants to translate international learning into measurable local impact. How the Fellowship Works Applicants begin by identifying an issue they are passionate about improving. Once selected, Fellows explore how similar issues are being addressed internationally by engaging with experts, organizations, institutions, practitioners, and innovators. Following their research, Fellows return to share their findings, implement new ideas, and contribute to positive change within their sectors and communities. This practical approach ensures that knowledge gained through the Fellowship benefits society well beyond the individual participant. Application Timeline Interested applicants should take note of the official application period: Applications Open: 1st September 2026 Application Deadline: 20th October 2026 Prospective applicants are encouraged to prepare their ideas early and register for application alerts to receive updates regarding the application process. Preparing a Strong Application Although detailed application guidance is provided separately by the Churchill Fellowship, prospective applicants should begin preparing by: Identifying an important issue they want to address. Demonstrating a genuine commitment to creating change. Researching existing challenges within their community or professional sector. Developing a clear vision of the knowledge they wish to gain internationally. Explaining how the Fellowship will create lasting impact after completion. Preparing examples of leadership, initiative, or community engagement. Reviewing the Fellowship s current programme areas to ensure alignment. APPLY HERE Why This Fellowship Matters Many social challenges require fresh thinking and practical solutions. The Churchill Fellowship recognizes that some of the best ideas can emerge through international collaboration and shared learning. By supporting passionate individuals to learn from global leaders, the Fellowship strengthens communities, encourages innovation, and creates lasting improvements across numerous sectors. Whether addressing education, climate change, healthcare, social inclusion, entrepreneurship, or community development, Churchill Fellows become part of a growing movement dedicated to positive change. Visit HERE for more information about the Become a Churchill Fellow 2026–2027 Fellowship. Stay Updated Individuals interested in applying are encouraged to sign up for the Fellowship s application alerts to receive notifications about application opening dates, programme updates, and additional guidance before the next application cycle begins. Deadline 20th October 2026. Conclusion The Churchill Fellowship represents an exceptional opportunity for individuals who are committed to solving real-world problems through international learning and collaboration. Rather than offering a traditional academic experience, the Fellowship empowers changemakers to explore innovative solutions from around the world and translate them into meaningful action within their own communities. If you have a strong vision for creating positive impact and are eager to learn from global experts, the Churchill Fellowship could be the ideal platform to turn your ideas into lasting change. With applications opening on 1st September 2026 and closing on 20th October 2026 , prospective applicants should begin preparing early to maximize their chances of success. title: Aspire Leadership Accelerator Powered by AI 2026: Transform Your Leadership, AI, and Career Skills in Just 8 Weeks

title: Council of Europe Youth Advocacy for Democracy and Human Rights Training Course 2026 (Fully Funded) – Apply by 14 August
summary: The Council of Europe Youth Department is inviting applications for the third edition of the Youth Advocacy for Democracy and Human Rights Training Course , which will take place at the European Youth Centre Strasbourg, France , from 27 September to 4 October 2026 . Organized under the Youth Revitalising Democracy Project , this fully funded international training programme is designed to strengthen the advocacy skills of young activists, youth leaders, and members of youth civil society organizations who are committed to promoting democracy, human rights, and meaningful youth participation in public decision-making. The training course will be held alongside the Plenary Session of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe , providing participants with a unique opportunity to gain insights into democratic institutions while learning practical advocacy strategies from experts and peers. If you are passionate about advancing democratic values, protecting human rights, and increasing youth participation in governance, this is an excellent opportunity to build your skills, expand your network, and contribute to positive democratic change. About the Training Course The Youth Advocacy for Democracy and Human Rights Training Course forms part of the Council of Europe Youth Department s broader efforts to strengthen youth engagement in democratic life. The programme recognizes that young people and youth organizations play an essential role in promoting democracy, defending human rights, and ensuring that youth perspectives are reflected in policy-making at local, national, and international levels. Through interactive learning, practical exercises, peer exchange, and engagement with Council of Europe institutions, participants will strengthen their ability to design and implement effective advocacy initiatives that promote democratic participation and human rights. The course also contributes directly to the objectives of the Youth Revitalising Democracy Project , which seeks to remove barriers to youth participation in politics and strengthen structures that enable young people to influence public decision-making. Aim of the Programme The primary aim of the training course is to strengthen the competencies of youth civil society representatives and young activists in advocating for: Democracy Human rights Youth participation Implementation of Council of Europe standards Inclusive public policies Youth representation in decision-making processes Participants will also explore ways to integrate youth perspectives across the work of the Council of Europe while promoting democratic values within their own communities and countries. Objectives of the Training Course Throughout the programme, participants will work toward achieving several important learning objectives, including: 1. Understanding the Council of Europe Participants will gain a comprehensive understanding of: The Council of Europe Its institutions Democratic governance structures Human rights standards Youth participation mechanisms 2. Strengthening Advocacy Skills The programme will help participants: Develop human rights-based advocacy skills. Design effective advocacy strategies. Plan advocacy campaigns. Build practical advocacy competencies. Influence policy processes. 3. Learning from Good Practices Participants will exchange experiences and learn from successful examples of: Human rights advocacy Democratic participation Youth engagement Civic activism Collaboration with policymakers Youth participation structures 4. Engaging with the Youth Revitalising Democracy Project The training will introduce participants to the ongoing work of the Council of Europe Youth Department and provide opportunities to contribute to future initiatives under the Youth Revitalising Democracy Project. 5. Developing Joint Advocacy Initiatives Participants will collaborate to design common advocacy actions that contribute to: Increasing youth participation in elections. Removing barriers preventing young people from running for public office. Strengthening youth participation in democratic decision-making. Expanding the implementation of Council of Europe democratic standards. What Participants Will Learn The programme combines theoretical knowledge with practical skills development. Participants can expect sessions covering topics such as: Democracy and democratic institutions Human rights advocacy Youth participation in governance Policy influence Advocacy strategy development Campaign planning Working with decision-makers Coalition building Civic engagement Peer learning and networking Practical Information The training course will take place: Venue European Youth Centre Strasbourg Strasbourg, France Programme Dates 27 September – 4 October 2026 The programme dates include both arrival and departure days. Financial Support The Council of Europe will cover participants major programme expenses in accordance with its financial regulations. Support includes: Travel costs Visa expenses Accommodation Meals during the programme This financial support enables selected participants to fully engage in the learning experience without worrying about major participation costs. Why You Should Apply Participating in this programme provides an opportunity to: Develop advanced advocacy skills. Strengthen your understanding of democracy and human rights. Learn directly from Council of Europe experts. Connect with youth leaders from different countries. Exchange experiences with fellow activists. Expand your international professional network. Contribute to future democratic initiatives. Become part of the Council of Europe s youth engagement efforts. Who Should Apply? The programme is particularly suitable for: Young activists Youth advocates Human rights defenders Youth organization representatives Civil society actors Youth workers Democracy promoters Community organizers Emerging youth leaders Applicants should have a demonstrated interest in promoting democracy, protecting human rights, and strengthening youth participation in public life. Application Process Interested applicants must complete the official online application form before the deadline. Applicants are encouraged to prepare their applications early to avoid last-minute technical issues. Only complete applications submitted before the deadline will be considered. Important Dates Activity Date Application Deadline 14 August 2026 (14:00 Strasbourg Time) Training Course 27 September – 4 October 2026 For More Information Applicants are encouraged to visit the official Council of Europe Youth Department webpage to access the concept note, review the full eligibility requirements, and complete the online application form. The official page also provides detailed information about the programme objectives, participant profile, financial arrangements, and application process. For any additional questions regarding the programme or the application process, prospective applicants should contact the Council of Europe Youth Department . Conclusion The Council of Europe Youth Advocacy for Democracy and Human Rights Training Course 2026 offers an exceptional opportunity for young activists and civil society leaders to strengthen their advocacy skills, deepen their understanding of democratic governance and human rights, and join an international network of committed changemakers. With travel, accommodation, meals, and visa costs covered, participants can fully focus on learning, networking, and developing practical advocacy initiatives that promote democracy and youth participation. If you are passionate about creating positive democratic change, be sure to submit your application before the 14 August 2026 deadline. title: CAPSHA South-South Collaboration Innovation Pitch Challenge 2026: Up to USD 15,000 Grants for Innovative Agricultural Capacity-Sharing Partnerships
summary: The CAPSHA South-South Collaboration Innovation Pitch Challenge 2026 is an innovation funding opportunity designed to support creative, demand-driven partnerships that strengthen agricultural research, extension, education, and innovation systems across Africa, Asia, and Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC) . The challenge is organized under the CGIAR Capacity Sharing (CapSha) Accelerator , which promotes a new model of collaboration focused on equitable partnerships, shared knowledge creation, mutual learning, and long-term institutional transformation. Unlike traditional capacity-building approaches where knowledge is viewed as something transferred from one organization to another, the CapSha Accelerator recognizes that sustainable innovation emerges when institutions collaborate as equal partners. Through this challenge, participants are invited to submit innovative ideas that can improve capacity-sharing approaches between CGIAR and National Agricultural Research Extension and Education Systems (NAREES) . Selected winners will receive grants of up to USD 15,000 to implement their proposed initiatives and contribute to stronger, more resilient, and inclusive food, land, and water systems. Opportunity Category Category: Grant / Innovation Challenge The CAPSHA South-South Collaboration Innovation Pitch Challenge provides financial support through competitive grants awarded to selected innovative partnership proposals. About the CAPSHA Accelerator National Agricultural Research Extension and Education Systems (NAREES) play a critical role in advancing sustainable agricultural development, food security, climate resilience, and rural livelihoods. However, today s global challenges require more than traditional knowledge-sharing methods. Increasing pressures from: Climate change Food insecurity Natural resource challenges Nutrition concerns Changing rural livelihoods The need for sustainable agricultural systems require new approaches that encourage collaboration, innovation, and shared ownership. The CGIAR Capacity Sharing (CapSha) Accelerator promotes a partnership-based approach where CGIAR organizations and NAREES institutions work together to: Generate knowledge collaboratively. Exchange expertise and experiences. Adapt innovative solutions to local contexts. Strengthen institutional capacity. Build long-term networks for continuous learning. The Innovation Pitch Challenge seeks ideas that demonstrate how collaborative capacity-sharing models can transform agricultural research and innovation systems. Goal of the CAPSHA Innovation Pitch Challenge The overall goal of the challenge is to identify and support innovative, demand-driven capacity-sharing partnerships that strengthen national research and innovation systems while contributing to CGIAR’s long-term impact agenda. The initiative aims to encourage partnerships that create practical solutions for strengthening agricultural systems and improving collaboration between institutions across different regions. Specific Objectives of the Challenge The CAPSHA South-South Collaboration Innovation Pitch Challenge aims to: 1. Strengthen CGIAR and NAREES Collaboration The challenge seeks to improve engagement between CGIAR institutions and National Agricultural Research Extension and Education Systems by creating stronger partnerships based on shared priorities. 2. Identify Innovative and Scalable Opportunities The programme aims to discover ideas that have potential for: Short-term implementation. Medium-term expansion. Long-term investment and sustainability. 3. Promote Equitable Partnerships The challenge encourages co-creation between CGIAR and NAREES institutions, ensuring that all partners contribute knowledge, expertise, and solutions. 4. Advance South-South and North-South Knowledge Exchange The programme supports collaboration between institutions across: Africa. Asia. Latin America and the Caribbean. Northern and Southern research institutions. This promotes mutual learning and strengthens global agricultural innovation networks. 5. Develop Scalable Models for Agricultural Capacity Strengthening Selected ideas should contribute to stronger: Agricultural research systems. Extension services. Education programmes. Implementation capacities. 6. Build Sustainable Learning Networks The challenge aims to encourage Communities of Practice and long-term networks that continue knowledge exchange beyond individual projects. Funding Award The total available award budget for the challenge is: USD 45,000 Three grants will be awarded: Africa Region: USD 15,000 grant. Asia Region: USD 15,000 grant. Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC) Region: USD 15,000 grant. The highest-ranked candidate from each region will receive funding to implement their proposed innovation project. Eligible Project Ideas Applicants are encouraged to submit innovative concepts that demonstrate practical approaches to improving capacity sharing and agricultural innovation systems. Successful proposals should focus on ideas that: Address real challenges within agricultural research and innovation systems. Promote collaboration between institutions. Encourage knowledge exchange and mutual learning. Have potential for scaling and replication. Strengthen food, land, and water systems. Support sustainable development outcomes. Partnership Approach The challenge emphasizes collaboration rather than individual institutional efforts. Projects may involve partnerships between: CGIAR Centers. Universities in the Global North and Global South. Government agencies. Farmer producer organizations. Private sector organizations. Non-governmental organizations (NGOs). Development partners. Regional organizations. Who Can Apply? Eligible Applicants Applications must be led by a National Agricultural Research Extension and Education Systems (NAREES) institution from one of the following regions: Africa. Asia. Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC). The lead applicant institution may collaborate with additional partners, including research organizations, universities, government institutions, private sector actors, and development organizations. APPLY HERE Eligible Regions and Countries The opportunity is open to eligible institutions located in: African countries. Asian countries. Latin American and Caribbean countries. The provided information does not specify individual eligible countries; applicants should confirm eligibility according to their regional NAREES institution status. Eligible Participants The challenge is suitable for: Agricultural research institutions. National extension systems. Agricultural education institutions. Research and innovation organizations. Universities. Government agencies involved in agriculture. Development organizations working on food systems. Partner organizations collaborating with eligible NAREES institutions. Important Eligibility Requirement The application must be led by a NAREES institution. Other organizations may participate as partners but cannot replace the required lead applicant. Award Benefits Successful applicants will receive: Funding of up to USD 15,000 for selected regional winners. Support to implement innovative agricultural capacity-sharing initiatives. Opportunities to strengthen international partnerships. Increased visibility within agricultural research and innovation networks. Opportunities to contribute to sustainable food systems transformation. Application Timeline Application Period Applications are open from: 24 July 2026 to 7 August 2026 Deadline: 7 August 2026 at 23:59 Indian Standard Time (IST) Applicants must submit their proposals before the deadline. Late submissions may not be considered. Selection Timeline 24 July 2026: Application period opens. 7 August 2026: Application deadline. 13 August 2026: Selected candidates for the pitch side event will be contacted. Pitch Challenge Selection Process Submitted proposals will be evaluated based on their alignment with the objectives of the challenge and their ability to demonstrate innovative approaches to capacity sharing. The challenge focuses on identifying proposals that: Present practical and achievable solutions. Strengthen institutional partnerships. Demonstrate innovation. Support sustainable agricultural development. Create long-term value beyond the project period. How to Apply Applicants should prepare and submit innovative proposals according to the challenge requirements. Interested institutions should ensure that: The proposal is led by an eligible NAREES institution. The idea demonstrates strong collaboration potential. The project addresses capacity-sharing challenges. The proposal clearly explains expected outcomes and sustainability. Applicants should follow the official submission process provided by the CAPSHA Accelerator. Visit HERE to learn more about the CAPSHA South-South Collaboration Innovation Pitch Challenge 2026 Why Participate in the CAPSHA Innovation Pitch Challenge? The challenge provides an opportunity for agricultural institutions and partners to move beyond traditional capacity-building approaches and develop new models of collaboration. Through participation, organizations can: Strengthen agricultural innovation systems. Build international partnerships. Develop scalable solutions. Improve knowledge exchange. Support climate-resilient food systems. Contribute to sustainable rural development. The challenge recognizes that solving complex agricultural challenges requires cooperation between institutions, communities, researchers, and policymakers. Conclusion The CAPSHA South-South Collaboration Innovation Pitch Challenge 2026 represents an important opportunity for agricultural research institutions and partners across Africa, Asia, and Latin America and the Caribbean to develop innovative solutions for strengthening capacity sharing and collaboration. With grants of up to USD 15,000 , the challenge supports initiatives that promote equitable partnerships, knowledge exchange, and sustainable transformation of agricultural research and innovation systems. Eligible NAREES institutions and their partners are encouraged to submit innovative ideas that can contribute to stronger food systems, improved resilience, and long-term global collaboration before the 7 August 2026 deadline . title: Eric and Wendy Schmidt AI in Science Postdoctoral Fellowship at the University of Oxford 2026: Fully Funded Opportunity for Early-Career Researchers Applying Artificial Intelligence to STEM Research
summary: The Eric and Wendy Schmidt AI in Science Postdoctoral Fellowship at the University of Oxford is now accepting applications for its fifth round of funding , offering an exceptional opportunity for talented early-career researchers to combine cutting-edge Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques with groundbreaking scientific research. The fellowship is designed to support researchers in the mathematical, physical, life, and medical sciences who wish to integrate AI and machine learning into their research projects. Through this prestigious programme, fellows receive mentorship, access to Oxford s world-class research environment, and the opportunity to develop innovative interdisciplinary projects capable of transforming scientific discovery. Applications for the 2026 intake open on 3 August 2026 , with the submission deadline set for 16 October 2026 at 12:00 noon . About the Eric and Wendy Schmidt AI in Science Postdoctoral Fellowship Artificial Intelligence is rapidly reshaping scientific research across virtually every discipline. From accelerating drug discovery and improving climate modelling to solving complex mathematical problems and advancing biomedical research, AI has become an essential tool for modern science. Recognizing this transformative potential, the University of Oxford established the Eric and Wendy Schmidt AI in Science Postdoctoral Fellowship to help outstanding researchers apply AI and machine learning techniques to significant scientific challenges. Rather than requiring applicants to already be AI experts, the programme seeks researchers with strong scientific backgrounds and promising research ideas who are eager to learn how AI can significantly enhance their work. Throughout the fellowship, participants receive support to deepen their AI knowledge while working alongside leading scientists and AI specialists at Oxford. Objectives of the Fellowship The programme aims to: Support innovative interdisciplinary research that combines AI with STEM disciplines. Develop the next generation of researchers capable of applying AI to scientific discovery. Foster collaboration between AI researchers and scientists across Oxford s Mathematical, Physical, Life and Medical Sciences (MPLS) divisions. Encourage responsible and ethical applications of Artificial Intelligence in research. Build long-term research capacity in AI-enabled science. Who Can Apply? The fellowship welcomes outstanding researchers who meet the following eligibility requirements. Applicants must: Have completed, or be due to complete before the appointment date, a DPhil or PhD. Hold a doctoral degree in one of the following fields: Mathematical Sciences Physical Sciences Life Sciences Medical Sciences Demonstrate an innovative research idea that could significantly benefit from AI or machine learning techniques. Possess sufficient understanding of AI concepts to explain how AI could improve or expand their research. Show awareness of the ethical implications associated with AI applications. Secure the support of an Oxford faculty member (Principal Investigator) within an eligible MPLS department who is willing to host them throughout the fellowship. APPLY HERE AI Mentor Requirements Although not compulsory, applicants are strongly encouraged to identify an AI or Machine Learning academic mentor before applying. The mentor should: Be an Oxford faculty member or senior researcher. Have expertise in Artificial Intelligence or Machine Learning. Possess research experience relevant to the applicant s scientific discipline. Provide academic guidance throughout the fellowship. This mentorship structure ensures fellows receive both scientific and AI-specific support during their research. Fellowship Benefits Successful fellows will benefit from numerous professional and academic opportunities, including: Access to one of the world s leading research universities. Opportunity to conduct interdisciplinary AI-enabled scientific research. Mentorship from internationally recognized Oxford researchers. Training to strengthen AI and machine learning expertise. Collaboration across multiple scientific disciplines. Exposure to advanced research infrastructure and facilities. Opportunities to contribute to innovative scientific discoveries. Participation in Oxford s growing AI research ecosystem. Professional development as an independent researcher. Research Focus Applicants are encouraged to propose research projects demonstrating how Artificial Intelligence or Machine Learning can significantly improve scientific investigation. Potential research may involve: Mathematical Sciences Physical Sciences Biomedical Research Medical Sciences Life Sciences Computational Science Data-driven scientific discovery AI-assisted experimentation Scientific modelling Advanced data analysis Machine learning applications in STEM Projects should clearly explain how AI techniques will transform existing research methods or create entirely new research possibilities. Ethical Considerations Applicants are expected to demonstrate an understanding of the ethical implications of Artificial Intelligence. Applications should consider issues such as: Responsible AI use Transparency Research integrity Fairness Accountability Scientific reproducibility Ethical deployment of AI technologies Oxford emphasizes responsible innovation alongside scientific excellence. Application Process Applications are submitted through the University of Oxford s Internal Research Award Management System (IRAMS). Before beginning an application, candidates should: Consult the relevant departmental Research Facilitators. Confirm any departmental internal deadlines, as some departments may require earlier submissions. Prepare all required documents well in advance. Applicants already affiliated with Oxford can submit directly through IRAMS after selecting the correct fellowship scheme. Applicants from outside Oxford will receive assistance from the relevant departmental research support team in uploading their application to the IRAMS platform. Application Timeline Important dates include: Applications Open: 3 August 2026 Application Deadline: 16 October 2026 (12:00 noon) Interview Period: December 2026 (dates to be confirmed) Applicants are strongly encouraged to begin preparing early to allow sufficient time for institutional approvals and submission. Assessment Process Applications will be reviewed by a multidisciplinary academic panel. Selection will be based entirely on how well applicants demonstrate that they satisfy the published eligibility and assessment criteria. The review process includes: Academic evaluation Assessment of research quality Evaluation of the proposed AI integration Review of scientific innovation Shortlisting Interviews for selected candidates Applicants should remember that panel members may not be specialists in their exact scientific field or AI methodology. Therefore, proposals should: Clearly explain the scientific challenge. Describe the proposed AI techniques in accessible language. Demonstrate the broader significance of the research. Explain expected outcomes and impact. Panel decisions are final. Equality, Diversity and Inclusion The University of Oxford is committed to promoting equality, diversity, and inclusion throughout the fellowship application process. Applicants from diverse backgrounds are encouraged to apply. Further Information Applicants seeking additional information may contact the Programme Manager via: Email: saiis@dtc.ox.ac.uk Prospective applicants may also: Watch the programme s Open Day recording. Contact relevant academic departments within Oxford s MPLS Division to discuss research opportunities. Consult departmental Research Facilitators before beginning an application. Why You Should Apply The Eric and Wendy Schmidt AI in Science Postdoctoral Fellowship represents one of Oxford s flagship initiatives for advancing AI-enabled scientific discovery. It provides an exceptional platform for outstanding postdoctoral researchers to develop interdisciplinary expertise, collaborate with world-renowned academics, and pursue innovative research capable of addressing some of society s most complex scientific challenges. For researchers seeking to combine Artificial Intelligence with advanced STEM research while building an international academic career, this fellowship offers an outstanding opportunity to work within one of the world s most prestigious research environments. Visit HERE to learn more about the Eric and Wendy Schmidt AI in Science Postdoctoral Fellowship at the University of Oxford 2026 Application Deadline Applications open on 3 August 2026 . The deadline for submitting applications is 16 October 2026 at 12:00 noon . Prospective applicants are advised to begin preparations early and coordinate closely with their prospective Oxford host department before submitting their application. Conclusion The Eric and Wendy Schmidt AI in Science Postdoctoral Fellowship at the University of Oxford offers an unparalleled opportunity for early-career researchers to pioneer the integration of Artificial Intelligence into scientific research. By combining world-class mentorship, interdisciplinary collaboration, and AI-focused training, the fellowship empowers researchers to drive innovation across the mathematical, physical, life, and medical sciences. Eligible candidates with ambitious research ideas are encouraged to prepare strong proposals and submit their applications before the October 2026 deadline. title: SFU Climate Innovation Seed Funds 2026: Up to $100,000 Available to Advance Community-Centred Climate Research and Innovation
summary: Simon Fraser University (SFU) has officially launched the 2026 SFU Climate Innovation Seed Funds , providing $100,000 in total funding to accelerate innovative climate research that delivers meaningful impact for communities. Designed to support interdisciplinary collaboration, the funding helps transform promising early-stage ideas into practical climate solutions through partnerships between researchers, students, Indigenous Nations, governments, community organizations, NGOs, and industry. Building on the success of its inaugural funding round, the SFU Climate Innovation (CI) initiative continues to strengthen research-for-impact by investing in projects that address pressing climate challenges while promoting sustainability, resilience, equity, and community engagement. Researchers and graduate students interested in developing innovative climate solutions are encouraged to apply before the extended application deadline of 6 August 2026 . About the SFU Climate Innovation Seed Funds The SFU Climate Innovation Seed Funds are part of Simon Fraser University s commitment to advancing its strategic climate innovation research priorities. Rather than simply funding research projects, the initiative provides a complete ecosystem of support designed to help interdisciplinary teams move ideas toward implementation, attract future funding, and create lasting societal impact. The program encourages collaboration across faculties and disciplines while placing communities and Indigenous partners at the centre of research design and implementation. For 2026, a total of $100,000 has been allocated across three funding streams: Amplification Grants Catalyst Grants Pollinator Awards Together, these funding streams create a research pathway that nurtures emerging ideas, strengthens partnerships, supports graduate researchers, and positions projects for larger national and international funding opportunities. Why the SFU Climate Innovation Seed Funds Matter Addressing climate change requires collaboration across disciplines, sectors, and communities. The Seed Funds recognize that impactful climate solutions emerge when researchers work alongside those most affected by environmental challenges. The initiative focuses on supporting projects that: Promote interdisciplinary collaboration. Strengthen Indigenous-led climate action. Advance community-centred research. Encourage knowledge sharing. Support equitable climate innovation. Generate practical solutions for resilient and sustainable communities. Rather than funding research in isolation, SFU Climate Innovation provides long-term support that helps projects mature into large-scale initiatives capable of attracting significant external funding. Funding Streams Available 1. Amplification Grant The Amplification Grant is designed for interdisciplinary teams seeking to develop major collaborative climate research initiatives. Funding Available Two grants of up to $25,000 each. At least one award will support an Indigenous-led application. Purpose The grants support: Workshops Workshop series Partnership development Research agenda development Cross-sector collaboration Preparation of major grant applications Successful teams are expected to develop ambitious research programs capable of securing future funding from major organizations such as: New Frontiers in Research Fund (NFRF) SSHRC Partnership Grants Horizon Europe Philanthropic organizations Expected Outputs Awardees should produce: Comprehensive interdisciplinary research programs Funder-ready proposals Expanded research partnerships Community-centred climate research initiatives 2. Catalyst Grant Catalyst Grants are intended for interdisciplinary faculty teams already working with established community partners. Funding Available Two grants of $15,000 each. Purpose Catalyst Grants help researchers: Deepen community partnerships. Co-design innovative climate solutions. Strengthen interdisciplinary collaboration. Build pathways toward larger research grants. Projects may also include up to two embedded Pollinator Awards , allowing graduate students to contribute directly to research activities while gaining valuable interdisciplinary experience. 3. Pollinator Award The Pollinator Award supports graduate students participating in Catalyst Grant projects. Funding Available Four awards of $5,000 each. Purpose The award enables graduate students to: Conduct community-engaged climate research. Build interdisciplinary research skills. Gain mentorship from faculty. Participate in knowledge mobilization. Develop science communication skills. Receive grant-writing training. Students are expected to contribute their own research objectives while supporting the broader Catalyst project. Research-for-Impact Supports The Seed Funds provide much more than financial assistance. Award recipients gain access to a wide range of professional supports, including: Convening and Facilitation Delivered through the SFU Morris J. Wosk Centre for Dialogue, helping teams facilitate meaningful collaboration and co-design processes. Partnership Development Supported by the SFU Partnerships Hub, connecting researchers with: Communities Indigenous Nations Government agencies NGOs Industry partners Knowledge Mobilization The SFU Knowledge Mobilization Hub assists teams in ensuring research findings are translated into practical action through: Knowledge exchange Community engagement Research dissemination Impact-focused communication Grant Writing Support Researchers receive proposal development assistance through: Office of Research Services Institutional and Strategic Awards These services strengthen applications for future large-scale funding opportunities. Capacity Building The Community-engaged Research Initiative (CERi) provides training on: Ethical community engagement Indigenous collaboration Community-centred research Cultural competency Partnership development Additional supports include science communication training, networking opportunities, interdisciplinary forums, and communications assistance. Who Can Apply? The program welcomes applications from several categories of participants. Researchers Multi-faculty interdisciplinary teams. Led by SFU faculty members. Working across multiple disciplines. Graduate Students Students seeking: Interdisciplinary research experience. Community-engaged learning. Climate research mentorship. Partners Collaborating organizations may include: Indigenous Nations Community organizations Government bodies NGOs Industry Academic institutions Eligibility Requirements Amplification Grant Applicants should: Lead interdisciplinary research. Develop collaborative climate research agendas. Convene diverse stakeholders. Prepare proposals for major future grants. Catalyst Grant Applicants must: Include faculty from at least two non-adjacent disciplines. Demonstrate established community partnerships. Focus on collaborative climate innovation. Pollinator Award Graduate student applicants must: Be enrolled at SFU. Be linked to a Catalyst Grant. Demonstrate interdisciplinary research. Include equity, diversity and inclusion considerations. Eligible Expenses Funding may support: Student stipends Research activities Community engagement Travel Workshops Knowledge mobilization Convening activities Climate research implementation Ineligible Expenses Funding cannot be used for: Existing administrative costs Personnel costs unrelated to the project Gifts Entertainment expenses Assessment Criteria Applications will be evaluated based on: Interdisciplinary Collaboration Projects should demonstrate meaningful collaboration across multiple disciplines. Community Co-Creation Successful proposals should show authentic partnerships with communities and Indigenous Nations. Innovation Projects should introduce creative approaches to addressing climate challenges. Feasibility Applicants must present realistic implementation plans. Systems-Level Impact Reviewers will assess the project s potential social, environmental, economic, and health benefits. Equity and Inclusion Projects should reflect multiple perspectives and demonstrate reflexive, equitable research practices. Application Process Applications are reviewed by the SFU Climate Innovation Advisory Group, which includes representatives from: SFU faculty Students Government Community organizations Funding agencies Applicants must complete the relevant application form and submit all required documents by email. Important Dates Activity Date Applications Open 1 June 2026 Application Deadline 6 August 2026 (Extended from 31 July 2026) Successful Applicants Announced September 2026 For More Information Applicants are encouraged to visit the official SFU Climate Innovation Seed Funds webpage to learn more about the available funding streams, eligibility requirements, downloadable application forms, scoring rubrics, and research support resources. For questions regarding eligibility or the application process, contact: Skye Vallance Program Manager Email: climate_innovation@sfu.ca Prospective applicants should carefully review the appropriate application form and guidance before submitting their proposal to ensure all eligibility and submission requirements are met. Why You Should Apply The SFU Climate Innovation Seed Funds provide an outstanding opportunity for researchers, graduate students, and community partners to collaborate on innovative climate solutions that generate meaningful impact. Beyond financial support, recipients gain access to mentorship, grant development assistance, partnership-building opportunities, and knowledge mobilization resources that help transform early-stage ideas into scalable climate initiatives. Whether your focus is Indigenous climate leadership, sustainable communities, AI for climate action, renewable energy, resilience, or interdisciplinary environmental research, this initiative offers the support needed to move your project from concept to implementation. Conclusion The 2026 SFU Climate Innovation Seed Funds represent a significant investment in interdisciplinary climate research that prioritizes collaboration, community engagement, and real-world impact. By supporting researchers, graduate students, and partners working together across disciplines, the initiative helps develop practical solutions that contribute to resilient, low-carbon, and sustainable communities. Interested applicants should begin preparing their proposals early and submit their completed applications before the 6 August 2026 deadline to take advantage of this unique funding opportunity.
